title: Normalized tensor transport on complexes and K-flat localization
statement: Let k0 be a finite field, l a prime invertible in k0, and X any k0-scheme. Fix an additive native bifunctor T, additive in each parameter, with all cochain totals and a parameter adjunction making T(P,-) left adjoint to the specified native internal Hom(P,-). Fix a NativeWeilTensorRingedBridge b [def-sf-native-weil-tensor-ringed-bridge]. Then NativeWeilRingedTensorComplexes b T adj is inhabited: there is an underived comparison E(T(P,Q)) with EQ tensor EP whose inverse is fixed by the tensor-Hom adjunction and b.nativeHom; a natural total-complex comparison with the ringed total of (EQ,EP), with scalar (-1)^(pq) on the (p,q)-summand; transport of native acyclic-test K-flat complexes to ringed acyclic-test K-flat complexes; and localization of all native K-flat complexes at quasi-isomorphisms onto their actual unbounded derived category [def-sf-native-weil-tensor-presentation]. No derived tensor, derived symmetry or forgetting comparison is an input or conclusion.

proof.text: For each P transport the native tensor-Hom adjunction along b.native, use b.nativeHom, and use uniqueness of left adjoints. Compose with the sheaf braiding to order actual factors EQ,EP. The counit formula fixes uncurry; parameter naturality fixes naturality in both arguments.

proof.text: Extend this underived comparison termwise. Equivalences preserve coproducts. Exchange the two cochain directions with the Koszul factor (-1)^(pq); its differential identity gives the signed summand formula and naturality.

source.place: Native tensor model, geometric tensor part of steps 1 and 3; Stacks 06YS, 06YU, 0FPT

proof.text: The equivalence and its inverse preserve and reflect acyclicity. Every ringed acyclic test is in the essential image of the equivalence on complexes, so the total comparison identifies the native and ringed K-flat conditions. Transport ringed K-flat resolutions through the equivalence. Tensor respects chain homotopies; contractible complexes are K-flat and K-flat complexes are closed under cones and shifts. In the homotopy category replace the middle complex of each derived roof, and each common refinement witnessing equality, by a K-flat resolution. This proves full faithfulness of the localized K-flat inclusion. Resolutions give essential surjectivity. Composing with the homotopy quotient gives the stated localization of native complexes.
